question: What is the relationship between the degree of polymerization and the internalization efficiency of siRNA in T cells?
answer: The degree of polymerization (DP) significantly influences siRNA internalization efficiency in T cells, with optimal performance observed at intermediate chain lengths. For dG-series polymers, DP 20 and 30 achieved 60-90% internalization, while higher DPs reduced efficiency. PGON-series polymers (DP 20-60) maintained 60-80% internalization, with DP 40 and 60 outperforming dG-series counterparts at longer lengths. However, charge content—rather than DP alone—was the dominant factor, as polymers with ≥40 cationic charges showed comparable internalization regardless of backbone chemistry. Notably, PGON polymers exhibited higher cytotoxicity (40-50% viability at DP 40-60) despite similar complex size and charge, suggesting toxicity arises from post-internalization mechanisms rather than delivery efficiency.

### 1. **Summary of the Paper's Purpose**:
The purpose of this paper is to investigate how the structure of guanidinium-rich polymers, specifically those synthesized via ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP), influences the internalization and delivery of small interfering RNA (siRNA) into cells. By comparing two polymer scaffolds (imide vs. diester) with varying degrees of polymerization and charge content, the study aims to identify structural factors that optimize siRNA internalization while minimizing cytotoxicity, thereby contributing to the design of improved delivery systems.
